question.prompt:
Square \(ABCD\) has side length \(30.\) Point \(P\) lies inside the square so that \(AP=12\) and \(BP=26.\) The centroids of \(\triangle ABP,\) \(\triangle BCP,\) \(\triangle CDP,\) and \(\triangle DAP\) are the vertices of a convex quadrilateral. What is the area of that quadrilateral?

[Figure 1](figures/2018_AMC_12B_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The side midpoints are useful because each centroid lies on the median from \(P\) to one of those midpoints. Let \(M_1,M_2,M_3,M_4\) be the midpoints of \(AB,BC,CD,DA\), respectively, and let \(G_1,G_2,G_3,G_4\) be the corresponding triangle centroids.

A centroid divides a median in the ratio \(2:1\), measured from the vertex. Thus, for each \(i\),
\[
PG_i=\frac23 PM_i,
\]
with \(G_i\) on segment \(PM_i\). The same scaling centered at \(P\), with length factor \(2/3\), therefore sends the midpoint quadrilateral to the centroid quadrilateral. Both bases and heights scale by \(2/3\), so areas scale by \(4/9\).

The midpoint quadrilateral leaves four right triangles at the corners of the original square. Each has legs \(15\) and \(15\), since the square's side length is \(30\). Its area is therefore
\[
30^2-4\left(\frac12\cdot15\cdot15\right)=450.
\]
Consequently, the centroid quadrilateral has area
\[
\left(\frac23\right)^2\cdot450=\boxed{200}.
\]
This calculation works for every interior point \(P\), so the particular lengths \(AP=12\) and \(BP=26\) do not affect the area. The answer is \(\text{(C)}\).
solutions.title: Scale the side-midpoint quadrilateral

solutions.explanation:
Leave \(P\)'s coordinates unknown and calculate the centroids. The useful feature is that every centroid receives the same contribution from \(P\).

Choose coordinates
\[
A=(0,30),\quad B=(0,0),\quad
C=(30,0),\quad D=(30,30),
\]
and write \(P=(x,y)\), where \(0<x<30\) and \(0<y<30\). A triangle's centroid coordinates are the averages of its three vertex coordinates. This follows by locating the midpoint of a side and moving two thirds of the way along the median from the opposite vertex.

The centroids of \(ABP,BCP,CDP,DAP\), in that order, are therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
G_1&=\left(\frac x3,\frac y3+10\right),\\
G_2&=\left(\frac x3+10,\frac y3\right),\\
G_3&=\left(\frac x3+20,\frac y3+10\right),\\
G_4&=\left(\frac x3+10,\frac y3+20\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Their common offsets \(x/3\) and \(y/3\) affect only the location of the figure. The listed points are the four side midpoints of a square of side length \(20\).

Removing the four corner right triangles, each with legs \(10\), gives the centroid quadrilateral's area:
\[
20^2-4\left(\frac12\cdot10\cdot10\right)
=\boxed{200}.
\]
No value of \(x\) or \(y\) was needed, so the given distances from \(P\) do not change the result. The answer is \(\text{(C)}\).
solutions.title: Let the unknown coordinates cancel
